name: OddsRelay API
description:
The OddsRelay odds API: matched boards, the raw board, discovery, coverage and status, as served at `https://api.oddsrelay.io`. Every route is `GET`; a trailing slash is ignored; an unknown path is 404 `not_found`; any other method is 405 `method_not_allowed` (a `HEAD`'s 405 has no body). A request that carries a body (none is read) is answered with `Connection: close`, and its connection ends.

## Keys
Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`, never in the query string. Server keys start `or_live_`; browser and dashboard keys start `or_pub_`, answer only calls from their own website's `Origin` (else 403 `origin_not_allowed`), and get `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoing that exact origin (never `*`). A browser's CORS preflight (`OPTIONS` with an `Origin`) is answered 204. Keyless routes: `/healthz`, `/v2/status`, `/v2/coverage` without a key header, `/v2/openapi.json`.

## Order of checks
The per-address shield (429 `too_many_from_address`), the key (401), the account's flood cap (429 `too_many_requests`), a suspended account (403 `account_suspended`; `/v2/usage` still answers), a browser key's website (403), then the route's own checks, each described on its operation. Every refusal is free.

## Tokens
One token pool per account, reset monthly; a trial's pool is one-off, so its reset is the trial's end when that comes first. A call's price comes from the request (the product and its filters), never from the reply's size: `/v2/pricing` publishes the table, `quote=true` prices any data request for free, and discovery, `/v2/usage`, `/v2/pricing`, 304s, replies with no events and every refusal are free. A price above the balance is 402 `insufficient_tokens`. Every reply to a valid key carries `X-Tokens-Cost`, plus `X-Tokens-Used`, `-Remaining`, `-Limit` and `-Reset` whenever the balance is known (`unlimited` on an unlimited account).

## Flood cap
One cap per account, per 10 seconds and per minute (dashboard keys have their own), plus a cap on requests in flight. Every reply to a valid key after authentication carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `-Remaining` and `-Reset` for the window with fewer left; over it is 429 `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`. The front door also caps each address and the whole service: those 429s carry `Retry-After` and an EMPTY body with no `code`, as does its 502.

## Errors
Every JSON error is `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`, plus `type` on a scope 403, `valid` on the four unknown-value 400s and on the four `*_not_in_plan` 403s (`bookmaker_not_in_plan`, `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `exchange_not_in_plan`: outside your plan's bookmakers or your account's scope; `GET /v2/usage` shows the scope), `products` on an `unknown_market` that another product carries (the products that carry it), the balance fields on 402 and `reason`/`dashboard_url` on `account_suspended`. Branch on `code`. `request_id` equals the reply's `X-OddsRelay-Request-Id` (a 405 carries it in the body only).

## Account scope
An account can carry a scope: per product, the sports, markets, bookmakers and exchanges it may read (raw's one `bookmakers` list names venues of both kinds). A product outside it is 403 `not_in_key_scope` for every key on the account; a value a call names outside it is 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan` or `exchange_not_in_plan` with `valid` (the scope's list for that product), `quote=true` included; a filter the call leaves out is trimmed to the scope, before the price. `GET /v2/usage` shows the scope (`scope`, `scope_version`; both null when the account has none). A scope that cannot be applied answers every data route and keyed `/v2/coverage` 503 `temporarily_unavailable`, never the unscoped data.

## Strict inputs
Each route reads the parameters listed on it; any other parameter, or one sent twice, is 400 `bad_request` naming it. `region` is one lowercase code; missing means `uk`.

## Gzip
Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses): bodies over 1 kB are then gzip. A request that refuses gzip (`Accept-Encoding` naming `gzip` or `x-gzip` with `q=0`, `*;q=0` with no gzip above 0, or `identity` alone: Python's `urllib` and `http.client` send `identity` unless told otherwise) gets plain bodies, but `standard`, `dutching` and raw answer it 400. A request with no `Accept-Encoding` gets plain bodies: the front door decompresses them and keeps the gzip representation's `ETag`. `/healthz`, `/v2/status`, `/v2/health`, `/v2/usage`, quotes and errors are always plain.

## Caching
Data replies (never a `quote=true` price), `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events` and `/v2/bookmakers` carry `ETag`, a label of the decompressed content; send it as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged body is 304 with no body, free. Keyed replies are `Cache-Control: private, max-age=2, must-revalidate` and `Vary: Authorization, Accept-Encoding, Origin`.

## Freshness
`meta.processed_at` and `X-Processed-At` are a board's time; `X-OddsRelay-Version` is the publish instant of the board version served (epoch ms), the same on every route for one publish; `meta.last_seen` (matched boards) and `last_seen` (keyed `/v2/coverage`) are when each venue and sport was last read; raw's `last_update` is when a venue's market last changed. The API cuts no row for age, but a venue whose latest read is older than its own window (twice its longest recurring gap between reads, at most two minutes) is left off the boards until it is read again.

## Versions
`/v2` is frozen as of 2026-09-21: from that date it takes additions only, meaning a new route, parameter, field, value or code that a client coded against `/v2` can ignore. A breaking change is anything that client cannot ignore: a route, field, value or code removed or renamed, a type or meaning changed, a new required input, or a refusal where there was an answer. A client must accept fields, values and codes it does not know. A breaking change ships only under a new path, `/v3`, announced at least 6 months ahead by email and in the changelog, and `/v2` is kept for at least 12 months after `/v3` ships. Anything scheduled to end carries `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on its replies. Event ids are opaque, and an event's id never changes for its fixture: once an id has been served, every later answer for that fixture carries it. If two ids turn out to be one fixture, the one served first is kept, and the other is listed in the event's `previous_ids` and still answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds`. Changing a served id is a breaking change. `X-OddsRelay-Api-Version` equals `info.version`, on every reply but `/healthz`, a `HEAD`'s 405 and the empty-bodied 429s and 502; additions never change it, and a new label comes only with a new version path.
